subject: Media Literacy
title: The Roman Acta Diurna: First Newspaper
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Roman Acta Diurna: First Newspaper.

hook.text: In 59 BCE, Julius Caesar ordered daily news posted on stone tablets across Rome.

buildup.text: The Acta Diurna reported Senate decisions, military victories, births, and deaths.

discovery.text: This was arguably the world's first newspaper — public information for mass consumption.

twist.text: Caesar created it partly to bypass the Senate and speak directly to Roman citizens.

climax.text: From the very start, mass media was used by the powerful to shape public opinion.

punchline.text: The first newspaper was also the first spin.

quiz.question: Why did Caesar create the Acta Diurna?
options: To bypass the Senate and shape public opinion
